newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK foreign reserves US$65.9 bln at end Jan - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: HK foreign reserves US$65.9 bln at end Jan - HKMA.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Thursday the amount of foreign reserves held in the Exchange Fund, excluding unsettled forward transactions, stood at US$65.9 billion at the end of January.
This represents an increase of 3.3 percent from the US$63.8 billion at the end of December, the HKMA said in a statement.
The figure largely reflected the increase in foreign reserves held in the Exchange Fund as backing for additional banknotes issued ahead of the Lunar New Year on February 6-9, it said.
Including forward transactions to be settled, foreign reserves stood at US$71.1 billion at the end of January compared with US$69.6 billion at the end of December.

The HKMA, the territory's de facto central bank, said Thursday's statement was the first time it had moved to monthly disclosure of foreign reserves as part of the ongoing effort to increase transparency of its operations.
But an HKMA spokesman cautioned that "monthly figures are likely to show sharp seasonal variations".
